body.x: DummDumm Inc. (CEO Cheonglim Joo) announced its participation in the Global Media Meetup on September 1. The event, co-hosted by AVING News and U.S. tech media outlet Ubergizmo, focused on introducing the technologies and products of Korean startups to global markets, highlighting CES 2026 Innovation Award entries and participants to expand visibility and business opportunities.

Founded in 2023, DummDumm is a Korean startup offering drone-based environmental solutions. The company built an integrated platform for safe and cost-efficient water quality monitoring and sampling, expanding its business across R&D, manufacturing, sales, education, and maintenance. It also develops original technologies such as drone ground control systems (GCS), high-load smart winches, and real-time water quality sensors to enhance efficiency and safety in water resource management.

The company previously collaborated with K-water, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and the Korea Rural Community Corporation to complete pilot projects for water sampling and analysis in rivers, dams, and lakes. It also operates drone license and field education programs in collaboration with universities and institutions across Korea. Internationally, in February, it signed an MOU with Ratchaburi Province, Thailand, for drone-based water management cooperation.

body.cap: Hydro Hawk, DummDumm’s water sampling and analysis drone | Image by DummDumm

body.x: At CES 2026, DummDumm will showcase Hydro Hawk, a next-generation drone integrating five precision systems for water quality analysis and sampling. Built with carbon fiber and aluminum frames, it balances lightweight durability and stable flight even in strong winds. A patented high-load winch supports up to 30kg and can collect up to 4 liters of water samples with ±0.1m accuracy at depths of up to 30m.

Immediately after sampling, Hydro Hawk measures pH, electrical conductivity, and turbidity. Its sensors are enclosed in impact- and corrosion-resistant alloy cases, ensuring accuracy for repeated measurements. Data is synchronized in real time via ultra-fast 5G GCS, enabling immediate monitoring and response by management authorities.

The drone’s symmetrical design ensures stable flight and precise sampling in turbulent conditions, while its modular structure allows rapid replacement of winches, sensors, and batteries. This design improves operational efficiency and simplifies control for field operators.

Hydro Hawk is the world’s only fully autonomous 5G-based water analysis platform, replacing manual sampling and lab analysis with over 60% cost efficiency gains. It also eliminates the need to dispatch personnel directly to water sources, thereby reducing the risk of accidents and setting a new global standard for safe and efficient water management.

body.cap: Cheonglim Joo, CEO of DummDumm, delivers a presentation at the Global Media Meetup with Ubergizmo held at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on September 1 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The drone’s modular design and adaptable flight algorithms allow compliance with environmental and aviation regulations across different countries. Hydro Hawk also delivers fully traceable data that meets U.S. EPA and UN SDG 6 standards, helping users align with ESG commitments and regulatory requirements.

DummDumm aims to leverage CES 2026 to establish practical networks in North America. “The U.S. market, with the EPA tightening water data management regulations, is ideal for Hydro Hawk. It addresses the management of large rivers and lakes and supports climate response initiatives. CES 2026 will play an important role in expanding our global footprint,” said CEO Joo.

Ahead of CES, the company will also join accelerator programs in Germany and Finland, where EU water framework directives and ESG standards are among the world’s strictest. DummDumm plans to establish business bases in Europe by partnering with local organizations and securing pilot projects.

body.cap: Cheonglim Joo, CEO of DummDumm (left), and Hubert Nguyen, CTO of Ubergizmo (right), during an interview | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In Asia, the company is exploring collaboration with Japanese drone specialist LiberaWare. Japan, facing a rapidly aging population, is experiencing a growing demand for automated water management solutions. In Brazil, explosive demand for water monitoring in the Amazon basin and agricultural water management is creating opportunities. DummDumm plans to target ESG-driven industries, including agriculture, mining, and energy, across South America.

“Our CES 2026 debut will showcase DummDumm’s technology and achievements to a global audience. CES is more than just an exhibition—it’s the best opportunity to meet buyers, investors, and media worldwide and gain visibility for early-stage growth,” Joo said. “Starting with CES, we will continue participating in events like NextRise, ENVEX, and MWC, strengthening our brand in global water and environmental management and evolving into a global leader in drone-environment convergence solutions.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo runs Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries, focusing on electronics and technology. It covers major exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen, a former NVIDIA programming engineer and 3D graphics developer, attended the event and has reported annually from CES on global companies’ products and technologies.
